title: Kernel microbench results (H100 + A100) — FP8/INT8 sprint
content:
Doc/sheet hybrid (text tables). Microbench only: single-kernel / fused-kernel timing with pinned env. Use this to inform kernel registry + autoselect heuristics, but do not treat as end-to-end.

Last run batch (tag): microbench_run_2026-02-25a
Harness: runtime-perf-suite (fp8/int8 branch)
Git SHA (runtime): 9c1d7f3 (includes PR-19812 + PR-19827 + PR-19841; pre hotfix PR-19941)
Runner: benchmark-lab matrix runner

Environment (pinned):
- H100 SXM (80GB): Driver 550.54.14, CUDA 12.4, NCCL 2.21.5, Container redwood/runtime-perf:1.22.0-rc3
- A100 SXM (80GB): Driver 535.104.05, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.19.3, Container redwood/runtime-perf:1.22.0-rc3
- GPU clocks: locked (H100 1410 MHz mem / 1980 MHz sm; A100 1215 MHz mem / 1410 MHz sm)
- Power mgmt: persistence on; exclusive process
- NUMA pinning: on
- Warmup: 200 iters; Measurement: 1000 iters (unless noted)
- Stats: report median (p50) and p95 across measurement iterations; in us unless otherwise stated

Definitions:
- Prefill attention: prompt length = S (full attention over S tokens), output = S tokens
- Decode attention: single-step attention over KV length = S, query length = 1
- GEMM: Wqkv / Wo style matmul; report per-call kernel time (includes epilogue when fused)
- FP16 baseline: current production kernel path (fused where available)
- FP8 attention: FP8 path integrated behind runtime flag (fused attention kernel where supported)
- INT8 GEMM: INT8 matmul path with shape guardrails; fallback expected when constraints unmet

Quick takeaways (microbench-level):
1) H100: FP8 attention is a clear win in long-context prefill regimes (S>=1024) for common head_dim=128; modest/neutral for short prefill; can regress decode at very small batch due to launch/dispatch overhead if scheduler mix is decode-heavy.
2) H100: INT8 GEMM wins are largest for larger K/N (hidden sizes >= 8192) and batch>=4; limited/none for small batches due to quant/dequant + epilogue cost.
3) A100: FP8 attention path is mostly not a win (implementation is H100-optimized); INT8 GEMM sometimes wins but is sensitive to alignment constraints and epilogue fusion (fused bias+gelu is still better in FP16 for some shapes).
4) Biggest end-to-end gap risk: decode-heavy workloads with small batch (B=1) where microbench shows FP8 decode attention can be flat or slightly worse unless we interleave/batch enough.

================================================================================
TAB 1 — Attention microbench (prefill) — head_dim=128, num_heads varies with hidden
Notes: (a) Using fused attention where available; (b) All times are per-layer attention op.

Columns: GPU | Mode | hidden | heads | S (seq) | B | FP16 p50/p95 (us) | FP8 p50/p95 (us) | Speedup (p50)

H100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 128  | 1 |  92 /  98 |  94 / 101 | 0.98x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 512  | 1 | 310 / 330 | 275 / 296 | 1.13x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 1024 | 1 | 595 / 638 | 480 / 520 | 1.24x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 2048 | 1 | 1190 / 1270 | 860 / 930 | 1.38x

H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 128  | 1 | 165 / 176 | 168 / 182 | 0.98x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 512  | 1 | 560 / 600 | 500 / 545 | 1.12x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 1024 | 1 | 1085 / 1170 | 860 / 950 | 1.26x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 1 | 2140 / 2300 | 1540 / 1690 | 1.39x

H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 4 | 2055 / 2210 | 1375 / 1500 | 1.49x
H100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 8 | 2120 / 2295 | 1340 / 1485 | 1.58x

A100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 128  | 1 | 118 / 125 | 129 / 137 | 0.91x
A100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 512  | 1 | 410 / 432 | 425 / 452 | 0.96x
A100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 1024 | 1 | 800 / 848 | 820 / 880 | 0.98x
A100 | PrefillAttn | 4096 | 32 | 2048 | 1 | 1575 / 1670 | 1620 / 1755 | 0.97x

A100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 512  | 1 | 740 / 780 | 780 / 840 | 0.95x
A100 | PrefillAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 4 | 2780 / 2960 | 2855 / 3100 | 0.97x

Interpretation:
- H100: prefill benefits scale with S and B (more math to amortize overhead + better tensorcore utilization). Biggest gains at S>=2048, B>=4.
- A100: no meaningful wins; treat FP8 attention as H100-only candidate for now.

================================================================================
TAB 2 — Attention microbench (decode) — query_len=1, KV_len=S
Notes: These runs are most sensitive to launch overhead and cache residency.

Columns: GPU | Mode | hidden | heads | KV len S | B | FP16 p50/p95 (us) | FP8 p50/p95 (us) | Speedup (p50)

H100 | DecodeAttn | 4096 | 32 | 512  | 1 |  34 /  39 |  37 /  44 | 0.92x
H100 | DecodeAttn | 4096 | 32 | 2048 | 1 |  62 /  72 |  60 /  70 | 1.03x
H100 | DecodeAttn | 4096 | 32 | 8192 | 1 | 148 / 172 | 132 / 160 | 1.12x

H100 | DecodeAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 1 |  95 / 110 |  98 / 120 | 0.97x
H100 | DecodeAttn | 8192 | 64 | 8192 | 1 | 240 / 290 | 218 / 270 | 1.10x

H100 | DecodeAttn | 8192 | 64 | 2048 | 4 | 105 / 125 |  94 / 112 | 1.12x
H100 | DecodeAttn | 8192 | 64 | 8192 | 4 | 270 / 320 | 232 / 290 | 1.16x

A100 | DecodeAttn | 4096 | 32 | 2048 | 1 |  78 /  92 |  83 /  99 | 0.94x
A100 | DecodeAttn | 8192 | 64 | 8192 | 1 | 320 / 380 | 330 / 405 | 0.97x

Interpretation:
- H100: FP8 decode is only a win when KV is long OR when B is high enough. For B=1, KV<=2048, can be flat or slightly worse.
- Potential action: autoselect FP8 decode only when KV_len exceeds threshold (or when scheduler indicates adequate batching). Tie into ADR heuristics.

================================================================================
TAB 3 — GEMM microbench (Wqkv-style) — M = tokens*B, K=hidden, N=3*hidden
Notes: This proxies the heavy GEMM in prefill; decode GEMM is smaller (M=B).

Columns: GPU | hidden | M (tokens*B) | FP16 p50/p95 (us) | INT8 p50/p95 (us) | Speedup | Fallback?

H100 | 4096 | 128  |  82 /  88 |  79 /  86 | 1.04x | no
H100 | 4096 | 512  | 305 / 320 | 262 / 280 | 1.16x | no
H100 | 8192 | 128  | 165 / 175 | 160 / 172 | 1.03x | no
H100 | 8192 | 512  | 640 / 680 | 525 / 565 | 1.22x | no
H100 | 8192 | 2048 | 2480 / 2660 | 1880 / 2030 | 1.32x | no

A100 | 4096 | 128  | 110 / 118 | 114 / 124 | 0.96x | no
A100 | 4096 | 512  | 420 / 445 | 398 / 430 | 1.06x | no
A100 | 8192 | 512  | 890 / 940 | 815 / 875 | 1.09x | no
A100 | 8192 | 2048 | 3450 / 3650 | 3180 / 3450 | 1.08x | no

Interpretation:
- INT8 GEMM becomes more favorable as M increases (bigger prefill batches / longer prompts). For small M, FP16 often wins (esp A100).
- For H100, INT8 path looks promising for prefill-heavy workloads; still need to validate end-to-end due to quantization/dequant placement and fusion differences.

================================================================================
TAB 4 — GEMM microbench (MLP-style) — (B*tokens x hidden) * (hidden x 4hidden)
Notes: MLP often dominates token compute for certain models; fusion matters a lot.

Columns: GPU | hidden | expansion | M (tokens*B) | FP16 p50 (us) | INT8 p50 (us) | Speedup | Notes

H100 | 4096 | 4x | 128  | 120 | 118 | 1.02x | INT8 overhead cancels gains
H100 | 4096 | 4x | 512  | 465 | 392 | 1.19x | better utilization
H100 | 8192 | 4x | 512  | 980 | 760 | 1.29x | strong win if epilogue fused
H100 | 8192 | 4x | 2048 | 3800 | 2750 | 1.38x | best observed regime

A100 | 4096 | 4x | 512  | 610 | 585 | 1.04x | mild win
A100 | 8192 | 4x | 512  | 1320 | 1285 | 1.03x | essentially flat
A100 | 8192 | 4x | 2048 | 5200 | 4900 | 1.06x | small win; p95 variance higher

Interpretation:
- INT8 wins depend on fusion. Cases without fused activation/bias reduce wins considerably.
- H100 sees substantial wins in large hidden sizes with sufficient M.

================================================================================
TAB 5 — Launch config notes (what we recorded)
H100 FP8 attention:
- Selected kernel: fused_mha_fp8_tc_v3
- CTA tile: 128x128 (observed), stages=4
- Uses: TMA loads + FP8 tensor cores
- Sensitive to: head_dim (best at 128), alignment of KV cache (see PR-19871 edge case), and decode batch size

H100 INT8 GEMM:
- Selected kernel: cutlass_int8_gemm_tc_sm90
- Requires: K multiple of 32, N multiple of 64, aligned input strides; otherwise fallback to FP16
- Epilogue: bias-add fused in most cases; gelu fusion still inconsistent across shapes

A100 paths:
- FP8 attention kernel currently not competitive (no sm90 features; extra conversion overhead)
- INT8 GEMM uses sm80 tensorcore int8 but often loses to well-tuned FP16 fused kernels for small M

================================================================================
Anomalies / variance notes (carryover into harness work):
- H100 variance spike when clocks not locked and node was shared (see Slack thread 1776408450). With exclusive + locked clocks, p95-p50 narrowed from ~18% to ~6% on decode.
- One case: H100 DecodeAttn hidden=8192, KV=2048, B=1 showed p95 spikes correlated with CPU preemption; fixed by pinning runner threads + raising process priority in runner.
- INT8 correctness failure previously seen for misaligned shapes (now guarded; see Slack 1776412331). Microbench suite includes negative tests to ensure fallback.

Recommendations (for kernel registry/autoselect v0):
1) H100:
   - Enable FP8 attention for prefill when S>=1024 OR (S>=512 and B>=4), head_dim=128, hidden in {4096, 5120, 8192}.
   - For decode, enable FP8 only when KV_len>=4096 OR B>=4; otherwise prefer FP16 to avoid small-batch regressions.
   - INT8 GEMM: consider enabling for prefill-heavy shapes when M>=512 and hidden>=4096; keep conservative for decode (M=B) unless B large.
2) A100:
   - Keep FP8 attention disabled by default.
   - INT8 GEMM optional: allow in opt-in mode; require shape alignment + perf canary gates.

Next actions / TODO:
- Re-run key decode cases after PR-19871 (KV cache alignment fix) and PR-19911 (scheduler knob defaults) to see if B=1 decode regressions are mitigated by better batching.
- Add additional head_dim coverage: 64 and 80 (some top hosted models differ).
- Capture Nsight traces for top 3 win and top 3 loss cases (requested in Slack 1776425512); attach trace ids here once uploaded.

Appendix — exact command template (microbench harness):
- runtime-perf microbench runner: ./perf/microbench --gpu=<h100|a100> --kernel=<attn|gemm> --mode=<fp16|fp8|int8> --hidden=8192 --heads=64 --head_dim=128 --seq=2048 --batch=4 --warmup=200 --iters=1000 --lock_clocks=1 --export_json=1

End.
